problem: Existing surveys on world models for embodied AI are organized by application domain or learning paradigm, and overlook the architectural question of how world models should be structurally integrated with policies in vision-language-action (VLA) and navigation systems.
motivation: World models let agents learn efficiently and plan by simulating environment dynamics, and VLA and navigation systems increasingly need them to link multimodal perception, language understanding and sequential decision-making. A structural view of integration makes trade-offs between designs explicit and gives design guidance.
key_idea: Introduce an integration-centric taxonomy of world models in VLA and navigation with three architectural paradigms: modular, sequential (plan-then-execute), and unified (end-to-end prediction and action).
insight: Per the abstract, the paradigms trade off differently: modular designs excel in interpretability, sequential ones in hierarchical reasoning, and unified ones in tight prediction-control coordination. No experiments or ablations are available since only the abstract was provided, so deeper insight cannot be extracted.
method: Modular Architectures: the world model and the policy are distinct modules, with the world model used for prediction or simulation and the policy for action.
Sequential Architectures: hierarchical plan-then-execute workflows, where the world model first imagines or plans and a separate stage executes.
Unified Architectures: world prediction and action generation fused in a single end-to-end network.
Trade-off analysis: comparison of the three paradigms on interpretability, hierarchical reasoning and prediction-control coordination, leading to future directions and architectural principles.
numbers_note: abstract only; survey paper with no reported results
results: This is a survey with no quantitative results. It contributes the three-paradigm integration-centric taxonomy and an analysis of the trade-offs between them.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so coverage, the specific papers classified and the depth of analysis cannot be verified.
The three-way taxonomy may blur for hybrid systems, and the survey provides no quantitative comparison across paradigms.
compares_to: existing world-model surveys organized by application domain or learning paradigm
